messages.content: I want an API that takes an IP address and returns company data with contact information if available.

headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Here are a few well‑known APIs that let you look up company (organization) data and, where possible, return contact details for the entity associated with an IP address: | Service | Key Features | Typical Contact Fields Returned | Notes | |---------|--------------|---------------------------------|-------| | **IPinfo.io** | • Returns `org` (organization name), `asn`, `country`, `region`, `city`, `postal`, `timezone`, `latitude/longitude`.
• Optional “Enterprise” plan adds `company` object with `name`, `domain`, `phone`, `website`, `logo`, `description`. | `name`, `domain`, `phone`, `website`, `logo`, `description` | Requires a paid plan for the full company profile. | | **ipdata.co** | • Provides `organization`, `asn`, `country`, `city`, `region`, `postal`, `latitude/longitude`.
• Enterprise tier offers `company` object with `name`, `domain`, `phone`, `website`, `logo`, `description`. | Same as above | Free tier limited to 50k requests/month; paid tiers unlock richer data. | | **ipstack.com** | • Gives `organization`, `asn`, `country_name`, `region_name`, `city`, `zip`, `latitude/longitude`.
• Premium plan adds `company` object with `name`, `domain`, `phone`, `website`, `logo`, `description`. | Same as above | Free tier limited to 10k requests/month. | | **MaxMind GeoIP2 / GeoLite2** | • GeoLite2 (free) returns `organization` (ISP/ASN).
• GeoIP2 (paid) returns `organization`, `asn`, `country`, `city`, `postal`, `latitude/longitude`. | `organization` (ISP/ASN) – no direct contact info. | No direct company contact fields; you’d need to cross‑reference with another database. | | **AbuseIPDB** | • Returns `abuseConfidenceScore`, `countryCode`, `isPublicProxy`, `isTorExitNode`, `isAnonymousProxy`, `isHostingProvider`, `isThreat`, `isSuspicious`.
• Optional “Enterprise” plan returns `company` object with `name`, `domain`, `phone`, `website`, `logo`, `description`. | Same as above | Focuses on abuse reports; contact info only on paid tier. | | **IP2Location** | • Provides `org`, `asn`, `country`, `region`, `city`, `postal`, `latitude/longitude`.
• Premium database includes `company` object with `name`, `domain`, `phone`, `website`, `logo`, `description`. | Same as above | Requires a paid database download. | ### How to Use (Example with IPinfo) ```python import requests ip = "8.8.8.8" api_key = "YOUR_IPINFO_TOKEN" # Replace with your token url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json" headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"} response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=5) data = response.json() print(data.get("org")) # e.g., "AS15169 Google LLC" print(data.get("company", {})) # Enterprise data: name, domain, phone, etc. ``` ### Choosing the Right Plan - **Free Tiers**: Good for low‑volume or testing; usually only return the organization name and ASN. - **Paid Tiers**: Unlock the `company` object with contact details. Prices vary (e.g., IPinfo starts at $50/month for 50k requests, ipdata at $99/month for 100k requests). - **Enterprise**: For high‑volume or specialized data (e.g., additional fields, higher rate limits). ### Things to Keep in Mind 1. **Accuracy**: The “company” data is often derived from WHOIS or public registries; it may not always be up‑to‑date. 2. **Rate Limits**: Free plans usually cap at 10k–50k requests/month; paid plans raise this limit. 3. **Legal & Privacy**: Ensure compliance with GDPR or other privacy regulations when using or storing contact data. If you need a quick, no‑cost solution for a small project, start with the free tier of IPinfo or ipdata and upgrade once you confirm the data quality meets your needs.
